Ruling 2026-11-14: Santé members order only through the Santé Mobile App; the member dashboard is for training, media, promos, announcements and live trainings

Said by Coach Ed in the Manager session, 2026-11-14 (Manila), reviewing the meyqh local preview.

His words: "this dashboard is intended for trainings, media library in promoting the products, special promo by the sante subscribers, announcements, and live trainings. the only order here is the membership pack it purchase. can you review again the ruling i made if they can purchase members price here? if I ruled yes, removed it. all orders, personal or dropship will be made thru Sante mobile app."

Manager's check: he had ruled yes. Task z8uq9meyqm (his spec) kept the web shop open to a signed-in member at member price, shipping to their own saved address. This ruling removes that.

What it means:
A signed-in Santé member cannot place a product order on the website, at member price or any price. Personal and dropship orders both go through the Santé Mobile App. Member-price checkout on the web is removed, and z8uq9meyqm is redirected to "block member web checkout and point to the Santé Mobile App".
The only purchase a member makes on the site is the Membership Pack.
Manager's reading, labelled as its own: the guest/non-member SRP storefront flow stays as separately approved. He may correct this.

Member dashboard, his layout (images 7 to 13 in the Manager session):
Menu: Dashboard, Training, Media Library, Affiliate Hub, Orders, a notification bell, then profile picture and name. The name opens a dropdown like TWCinc's: My Purchases (the Membership Pack purchase details), Account Settings, Help Center, Theme, Logout. "My Orders" and the separate Account, name and Logout items are removed.
Training: copy TWCinc University (courses, modules, lessons, progress, next live bootcamp), adapted to NegosyoOnline (ruling 1100430000520345).
Media Library: copy TWCinc's, with no Source filter (Santé only) and Santé's product categories.
Wider content: less left and right padding, like the TWCinc dashboard.
He asked whether members can have an affiliate link, with purchases through it shown in their Orders menu. SANTE answers that from the code first.

Supersedes: z8uq9meyqm's "own address + member price" rule; z8uq9meyqh's "exactly three cards" Training and its menu; the "no LMS/progress tracking" line of meyqh's out-of-scope.

A record only. It approves no migration, production or spending action.

RULING, Coach Ed, 2026-11-14, Manager session: "allow copying TWCinc code"

Context: he asked that the Santé process flow be exactly the same as TWCinc. He was offered the choice between "same process flow, fresh code" and "allow copying TWCinc code where it fits, minus secrets and deployment config", and he chose the second.

What this means for every role. It replaces the CLAUDE.md line "never copy its code ... wholesale" and the "Do not import TWC runtime models" line in task briefs, where they conflict:
TWCinc code may be copied and adapted into NegosyoOnline to reproduce TWCinc's process flow exactly: screens, step order, statuses, emails and events.
Never copied: secrets, keys, tokens, credentials, .env files, TWCinc data or fixtures with real customer data, and deployment or Railway config.
Copied code is adapted to NegosyoOnline:
site-scoped (every query filtered by site, no single-tenant assumptions);
NegosyoOnline's own settings names;
no import of a TWCinc package at runtime.
The usual rules still apply: approved scope, tests, cross-site isolation tests, the Supervisor's review, the local release checks and Coach Ed's approval for migrations, production and Railway variables.
Dependencies come in only when the copied code needs them, are added with uv, and are pinned.
Record the TWCinc source path of copied code in the PR or the branch notes.

The CLAUDE.md wording will be updated through the next backend release round.

Ruling 2026-11-13: for the next few months there is one staff account only, Coach Ed's admin account; staff users need no HQ page

Said by Coach Ed in the Manager session, 2026-11-13, after the HQ Supervisor found that removing the Django admin (Plan 11 PR 3, z8uq9mek62) leaves no HQ page to add or deactivate staff users (gap G1).

His words: "Regarding this staff users, I want to rule on this because in our launching or maybe in the next few months, there will only be one staff, which is me. Okay, so the user for that is the admin at negotioonline.com if you want to ask about the login. Okay, so I want you to rule on this one because it's been asking a lot about this. So you need to take note that in the next few months, there's only one staff account, which is the admin@negotioonline.com."

What it means:
At launch and for the next few months there is exactly one staff (HQ) account, Coach Ed's, the "admin" address he named (spoken as admin@negotioonline.com; the manager reads it as the admin address on the NegosyoOnline domain, spelling as he confirms it). No second staff user is planned.
So G1 is settled: no HQ "Staff users" page and no staff add/deactivate feature is built now. Removing the Django admin goes ahead; creating or locking a staff account, if ever needed, is done by the existing commands (createsuperuser, then admin_identity add / admin_identity disable), with a runbook line in PR 3.
Supervisors do not ask again about staff-user management, multiple staff roles or staff invitations; such work is after launch unless he rules otherwise. When a session needs the HQ sign-in, it is this one account, and the sign-in code goes to Coach Ed.

Affects: HQ Supervisor (Plan 11 PR 3); supervisor brief (staff accounts); any task assuming several staff users. Not yet in the briefs; goes in with the next briefs PR.

Ruling 2026-11-13: the release builders run every CI check locally first, so a release PR is never opened to fail

Said by Coach Ed in the Manager session, 2026-11-13, right after ruling 1100430000509929 (the release train).

His words: "So you need to take note also that in our release builder front end and back end, it must conduct a test in our local so that we are sure that when it create or open a PR, there will be no bad or disapproval of of the PR. Okay, that is very important, and we need to put it in record or in our brief or in our handovers or in our memory in order for us to continue this one, because I don't want to repeat myself in the next manager or in the next supervisors, right? So it must be engraved in their instructions. So because this will be our new workflow."

What it means:
Before a release branch is pushed or a release PR is opened, the Release Builder (backend and frontend) runs locally every check the repository's CI runs, on the combined release branch, and all must pass. No push, no PR, until they do.
Backend: the full suite on SQLite; the full suite on a throwaway local PostgreSQL with a local Redis (localhost only); manage.py check; makemigrations --check; every migration applied on a fresh PostgreSQL; and any other job in the CI workflow.
Frontend: for every app the CI matrix runs (site, dash, storefronts, hq): install with the frozen lockfile, lint, tests, build, with the CI's Node and pnpm versions.
The release PR body lists the checks run and their results. The manager says "go: create the PR now" only after reading that all of them passed.
A failure found locally drops the offending branch from the round (back to its Supervisor); it is never fixed inside the release branch. A CI failure after a green local run is investigated before any re-run.
Supervisors still send only branches whose own local suite is green.

This is the standing release workflow. It must be carried into: the manager brief (sections 4 and 7), the supervisor and builder briefs (ready-branch reports instead of PRs), the handover-manager and handover-supervisor commands, and each Release Builder's standing instruction. Extends 1100430000509929.

Affects: manager, supervisor and builder briefs; handover commands; Release Builder instructions. Not yet in the briefs; goes in with the next briefs PR.

A record only. It approves no plan, build or gated action.

Ruling 2026-11-13: the manager runs a release train, one release builder session per repository, one combined PR per round

Said by Coach Ed in the Manager session, 2026-11-13.

His words, proposing it: "what I'm proposing right now is we will be creating a branch for managers, of course it's local, then they will merge it in our branch, then maybe we will be creating a builder for manager where it will consolidate all the updates from the supervisors, so that we will only be dealing with one PR every time there will be a request from our supervisors to open on PR."

His words, after the manager laid out the plan and asked for the ruling (the manager may run one release builder that only combines reviewed branches, owns the release branch per repository, and merges release PRs on green; production excluded): "Yes, I approve this proposal. I think we need two builders or session in order for it to merge the back end and of course for the front end. So I think we need two session for this one."

What it means:
Two standing release sessions under the manager: "Release Builder backend" and "Release Builder frontend" (Sonnet 5.5, medium). They write no feature code. Each round they cut a fresh release branch from main, merge each Supervisor's ready branch as its own merge commit, settle only trivial conflicts (lockfile re-lock, docs keep both sides) and send any feature-logic conflict back to the owning Supervisor, run the full local checks (backend: SQLite, PostgreSQL, Redis, makemigrations --check, migrate on a fresh PostgreSQL; frontend: tests, lint, build), then push and open one PR listing each branch, task and Supervisor.
Supervisors no longer open PRs or combine branches themselves: they report a ready branch (head SHA, local suite green, reviewed, local visual test passed where there is something to look at, ClickUp task) to the manager, who puts it in the next round.
A CI failure drops the offending branch from the round; it is never fixed inside the release PR. The manager merges a release PR when CI is green at its head and checks staging health; each Supervisor checks its own part on staging and keeps its ClickUp statuses. Staging visual tests stay Coach Ed's.
Rounds: when two or more branches are ready or one has waited half a day; at most two a day per repository; an approved hotfix goes alone, first.

Supersedes, for these two release sessions only: comment 1100430000508496 (the manager starts no builder) and the manager brief line that the manager edits no branch. Extends 1100430000509657 (batching) from one Supervisor's branches to all Supervisors'. Merge on green for release PRs is added to the manager; the Supervisors' three standing approvals are unchanged except that they no longer open PRs. Production is never covered.

Affects: manager brief sections 4, 6, 7; supervisor and builder briefs (PR creation); clickup-supervisor and clickup-builder commands. Not yet in the briefs; goes in with the next briefs PR.

A record only. It approves no plan, build, migration, variable, deploy or production action.

At production launch the staging database is moved once into production, so members keep their accounts and payments and only need to sign in at the new address. That move is a production action and needs his word then.
Real members sign in by email code; the Google client is still in Testing (three test users).

Ruling 2026-11-13: ready branches for the same repository go up as one PR

Said by Coach Ed in the Manager session, 2026-11-13, showing the NegosyoOnline Actions budget at $4.05 of $10.00.

His words: "by the way after you manages, our github actions up from 2usd to 4usd. can you make a plan also that we will be able to save money this! we still not in launch and we are already paying a log on our services. I suggest on this that if there are two or more queue for the PR, tell the supervisor to the merge in one so that the PR itself is only one action."

What it means:
When a Supervisor has two or more branches ready for the same repository, it combines them into one integration branch and opens one PR, instead of one PR per branch. The queue counts batches, not branches. A ready batch is never held for an unready branch. Local checks must be green before any push to a PR.

The manager's reading, labelled as its own: a backend PR costs about 20 to 25 CI minutes (the PR run plus the run on main after merge), a frontend PR about 2 to 3, so batching backend branches saves the most. Each branch in a batch still needs its own plan check and, where there is something to look at, the Supervisor's local visual test.

Unchanged: one open PR per repository; merge on green at the reviewed head; standing approvals.
